issues.description: Method de.tum.cit.ase.Farm.singFarmSongVerse(Animal): the problem statement text (problem_statement.md lines 112-115) explicitly instructs students to implement the helper method singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as public for easier testing. However, the UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 16-21) marks singFarmSongVerse as private (prefixed with a minus sign), the template implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 18) declares it as private (private void singFarmSongVerse(...)), and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java line 33) also declares it as private. This visibility mismatch (text says public, UML/template/solution use private) can confuse students about the required access level and may cause tests or external grading harnesses that expect a public helper to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the required visibility consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the template and solution Farm.java to declare the helper as public (change signature to public void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }) and update the UML in problem_statement.md to show a public method (+). Alternatively, if the helper should remain private, remove or change the sentence in the problem text that requires it to be public and ensure tests/harness do not rely on public access. Ensure tests, examples, and documentation all align with the chosen visibility.
